paper.title: Policy-Aware Design of Large-Scale Factorial Experiments

settings.name_in_paper: Fixed-budget policy selection in large-scale factorial experiments with low-rank (Tucker) effect tensor
unmapped: Arms are the K=d^m cells of an order-m tensor (m factors with d levels each); mean rewards form a tensor with Tucker multilinear rank (r,...,r) and mu_0-incoherence
Stage-I sampling is uniform over the active Cartesian design set; algorithm relies on a tensor-completion estimator with an entrywise sup-norm tail bound (Assumption 4/9)
settings.definition_quote: Let $\mu^\star := \max_{\bidx} \mathcal{T}_{\bidx}^\star$ ... The Simple Regret is defined as the expected optimality gap of the recommendation: \SR_N := \mathbb{E}_\pi[\mu_\star - \mu_{J_N}] ... We assume the noise terms $\xi_{\bidx}$ are independent sub-Gaussian random variables with mean zero and variance bounded by $\sigma^2$.

algorithms.name: Two-stage algorithm (tensor stage + vector stage Sequential Halving)

symbols.df: degrees of freedom m(dr - r^2) + r^m of the low-rank tensor
symbols.L_I: number of Stage-I tensor rounds (switch round)
symbols.p_min: minimum roundwise Stage-I sampling rate N_l/|A^(l)|
symbols.Tinf: max absolute entry of the true tensor
symbols.lambda_min: lower bound on smallest nonzero singular value across matricizations of active sub-tensors
symbols.K_II: number of arms surviving Stage I, (d/2^L_I)^m
symbols.L_II: number of Sequential Halving rounds, ceil(log2 K_II)

conditions: Tucker low-rank structure with mu_0-incoherence (Assumption 2), d_1=...=d_m=d, r_1=...=r_m=r
uniform sampling over active set with sigma^2-sub-Gaussian noise (Assumption 3)
tensor completion estimator satisfies sup-norm tail bound on every restricted active sub-tensor with uniform lambda_min (Assumptions 4 and 9)
d is a power of two (WLOG)
tuning: switch round L_I fixed in advance
Stage-II budget N_II = N - sum of Stage-I budgets

source.label: thm:TwoStage-gapind
source.quote: Then the simple regret satisfies: \mathrm{SReg}_N = O\!\left(\sigma\,\left[\sqrt{\tfrac{\df\,\Lsw^2\,\log d}{p_{\min}}\,\log \Lsw} \; \frac{\infnorm{\cT^\star}}{\lambda_{\min}} + \sqrt{\tfrac{\Kps\,\Lps}{\Nps}\,\log \Lps}\right]\right), where $\df = m(dr-r^2)+r^m$ is the degrees of freedom of the low-rank tensor model.

results.notes: Budget N is the horizon T. Compute marked polynomial assuming a polynomial-time tensor-completion routine (e.g. RGD), as the paper suggests.

bound.regime: p_min >= K_0 (sigma/lambda_min)^2 log(d) ||T*||_inf H_2I (m r + r^m/d_min) and N_II >= C_0 M_row(eps)

symbols.lambda_min: uniform lower bound on smallest nonzero singular value of active sub-tensors
symbols.Tinf: max absolute entry of the true tensor
symbols.H_2I: Stage-I row-gap hardness max_{2<=t<=d} t/Delta_t^2 with Delta_t = min_k (mu_{k,(1)} - mu_{k,(t)})
symbols.C_m: absolute constant from tensor completion tail bound

conditions: 1 <= L_I <= min{l'(eps), floor(log2(d/r))} where l'(eps) is the mode-wise pivot round
p_min >= K_0 (sigma/lambda_min)^2 log(d) ||T*||_inf H_2I (m r + r^m/d_min)
tuning: switch round L_I chosen satisfying the pivot-round constraint

source.label: thm:gap-dep
source.quote: the output $J_N$ of the two-stage algorithm satisfies the gap-dependent tail bound \Pr(\mu_\star-\mu_{J_N}>\eps) \le C_m\,\Lsw\,\exp(-\widetilde{\Theta}(\frac{p_{\min}\,\lambda_{\min}^{\,2}}{\sigma^2\,\infnorm{\cT^\star}\,H_{2,\mathrm{I}}})) + \exp(-\widetilde{\Theta}(\frac{\Nps}{H_{\mathrm{row}}(\eps)})) ... The notation $\widetilde{\Theta}(\cdot)$ hides only absolute constants and logarithmic factors in $d$.

results.notes: Bound on probability of selecting an eps-suboptimal arm (PAC-style tail), recorded as quantity 'other'. The Theta-tilde inside the exponents (hiding constants and log d factors) cannot be expressed; expression drops those constants and is marked O_tilde. Theorem statement uses ||T*||_inf (not squared) though the proof has the square.

cited_results.setting_description: Fixed-budget K-armed stochastic bandit with sigma^2-sub-Gaussian noise; tail of simple regret of Sequential Halving with budget N over L=ceil(log2 K) rounds: P(mu* - mu_J > x) <= 3 L exp(-x^2 N/(32 sigma^2 K L))
Unstructured K=d^m-armed fixed-budget simple regret (pure vector baseline)
